title: 1977 Greater London Council election
summary: The Conservatives, led by Horace Cutler, took control of the Greater London Council from Labour in a landslide, winning 64 of the 92 seats on 52.5% of the vote amid a slump in Labour's national fortunes. The Liberals lost both seats won in 1973, and the National Front polled 5.3% across London.
highlights: Conservatives sweep to control with 64 of 92 seats
Labour falls to 28 seats as its vote drops 14.5 points
The Liberals lose both of the seats they won in 1973
The National Front wins 5.3% but no seats

council.note: 92 single-member electoral divisions. From 1977 all aldermen left office and no further aldermen were appointed.
